units.function: open on a record crowd count, then derive the goal from the risk that count creates

original_instantiations: Last season the hall set a record for attendance. That many people at once makes getting everyone out much harder, so our goal is a plan that clears the building and still lets the response team in.
The venue drew a record crowd that season. A crowd that size raises the risk if something goes wrong, so the goal is a plan that empties the building while the response team still gets in fast.

units.source_excerpt: In 2018, the number of people in the Louvre was 10.8 million, creating a new high. At the same time, in the event of an emergency, such a large number of tourists will increase the difficulty of evacuation and raise the risk. Therefore, our goal is to design the Louvre's emergency evacuation plan.
units.reusable_pattern: In [year], [the count] was [number], creating a new high. Such a large number will increase the difficulty and raise the risk. Therefore, our goal is to [the task].
reusable_elements: occurrences: summary sheet, first paragraph.
stable function: earn the goal from a number rather than from a slogan.
pattern: creating a new high / raise the risk / Therefore, our goal is.
boundary: the number must be real and cited later; do not invent a record.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not treat a record crowd as proof that any plan is needed.
Do not copy the venue name or the visitor count.

units.function: report one number and immediately call the plan reliable because the number is short

original_instantiations: We also built a time model and found the shortest clearance for the largest crowd was 417.2 seconds. This result indicates that the plan is reliable.
A time model gave 417.2 seconds for the busiest case. That number, we say, shows the plan holds up.

units.source_excerpt: We also established an evacuation time model and found that the shortest evacuation time for the largest number of visitors in the library was 417.2 s. This result indicates that our evacuation plan is reliable.
units.reusable_pattern: We found that [the quantity] was [number]. This result indicates that our [plan] is reliable.
reusable_elements: occurrences: summary sheet, second paragraph.
stable function: turn a single computed time into a reliability claim.
pattern: this result indicates that ... is reliable.
boundary: the number needs a benchmark later; the sentence itself gives none.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not treat a short time as proof of reliability without a comparison.
Do not reuse the seconds or the building.

units.function: state a worked example as an assumption plus a result, then call the model reliable

original_instantiations: By assuming the trouble starts in one room on the lower floor and adding a new door near one stair, we get the best path for the response team and a shortest time of 130 seconds. This result shows the model is reliable.
We suppose the incident is in one named room and that a side door opens near one stair. The route and a time of 130 seconds follow, and we take that as the model working.

units.source_excerpt: By assuming an emergency in the 101 area of the -1F and adding a new exit near the B3 stairs of the 0F, the optimal path for the emergency personnel to reach the area and the shortest time of 130s are obtained. This result shows that our model is reliable.
units.reusable_pattern: By assuming [a scenario], [the route] and the shortest time of [number] are obtained. This result shows that our model is reliable.
reusable_elements: occurrences: summary sheet, third paragraph.
stable function: present one worked case as evidence the method runs.
pattern: by assuming X, Y and Z are obtained.
boundary: one scenario is an illustration, not a sweep.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not promote one assumed room into a general claim about all rooms.
Do not copy the room numbers or stair labels.

units.function: stack the danger of dense places, then declare the problem has unprecedented significance

original_instantiations: Dense places keep producing serious casualties, one of the major disasters people face. Hence, solving emergency evacuation in crowded areas has an unprecedented significance today.
Casualties in packed venues keep mounting, and this counts as one of the major disasters. Hence, getting people out of crowded places has a significance it did not have before.

units.source_excerpt: Due to the serious casualties caused by emergency emergencies in densely populated places, which is one of the major disasters faced by mankind. Hence, solving the problem of emergency evacuation in densely populated areas has its unprecedented significance in today's world.
units.reusable_pattern: Due to [the harm], which is one of the major disasters faced by mankind. Hence, solving [the problem] has its unprecedented significance.
reusable_elements: occurrences: section 1.1, first paragraph.
stable function: lift a local problem to a general urgency.
pattern: one of the major disasters / Hence / unprecedented significance.
boundary: the sentence is a fragment in the source; keep the cadence, do not repair it into a claim the paper did not make.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not use this to claim any evacuation paper is globally significant.
Do not copy the casualty wording as fact.

units.function: state the generic goal of an evacuation before naming the building

original_instantiations: In general, the goal of an evacuation is to have everyone leave as quickly and safely as possible.
Broadly, the aim is that all occupants get out, fast and unhurt.

units.source_excerpt: In general, the goal of evacuation is to have all occupants leave the building as quickly and safely as possible.
units.reusable_pattern: In general, the goal of [the task] is to have [everyone] [do the thing] as quickly and safely as possible.
reusable_elements: occurrences: section 1.1, second paragraph.
stable function: plant the objective before the case study.
pattern: in general, the goal is.
boundary: a generic goal must be followed by the specific constraints.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not stop at the generic goal; the paper's value is in the constraints that follow.

units.function: list the kinds of visitors, then say that variety is what makes the task hard

original_instantiations: The mix of visitors -- many languages, groups that travel together, and people who move slowly -- makes getting everyone out in a crisis even harder. As a result, a complete plan is necessary.
Visitors differ: languages, groups, and people who cannot use stairs. That mix makes an emergency exit harder, so a full plan is needed.

units.source_excerpt: The diversity of visitors -- speaking a variety of languages, groups traveling together, and disabled visitors -- makes evacuation in an emergency even more challenging. As a result, it is necessary for the Louvre to have a complete emergency evacuation plan.
units.reusable_pattern: The diversity of [people] -- [list] -- makes [the task] even more challenging. As a result, a complete plan is necessary.
reusable_elements: occurrences: section 1.1, third paragraph.
stable function: turn heterogeneity into the reason a single rule fails.
pattern: dash list, then makes X even more challenging.
boundary: each listed kind should reappear later as a modeled case.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim diversity always dominates other constraints.

units.function: state a tension between extra exits and security, then defer the choice to careful modeling

original_instantiations: Extra doors the public does not know would strengthen a plan, while their use would at the same time weaken security, since those doors are watched less than the main ones. Thus, when we build the model, we should think carefully about when and how any extra door gets used.
Doors the public never sees would help people leave, and would at the same time lower security. So the model has to decide, carefully, when such a door opens and for whom.

units.source_excerpt: While public awareness of these exit points could provide additional strength to an evacuation plan, their use would simultaneously cause security concerns due to the lower or limited security postures at these exits. Thus, when creating the model, we should consider carefully how to evacuate disabled visitors, when and how any additional exits might be utilized.
units.reusable_pattern: While [the benefit], [the same choice] would simultaneously cause [the cost]. Thus, we should consider carefully [the decision].
reusable_elements: occurrences: section 1.2, first task.
stable function: hold two opposing effects of one lever in one sentence.
pattern: while ... would simultaneously ... Thus, consider carefully.
boundary: the sentence names the decision; it does not make it.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not resolve the security tradeoff inside this sentence.

units.function: chain four data-to-result steps, each opening with a method phrase

original_instantiations: From the queue times the app shows, we get the head count at each hour. From the improved search, we get the best route out. Through the time model, we find the shortest clearance. From the improved shortest-path method, we get the route for the response team.
The app's queue times give the crowd by hour. The improved search gives the route. The time model gives the clearance. The improved path method gives the responders their way in.

units.source_excerpt: According to the current queuing time displayed by the APP "Affluences", we get different numbers of people at different times of the day. According to the improved ant colony optimization algorithm, we get the best evacuation route for tourists. Through our time model, we found the shortest time for visitors to evacuate. Based on the improved Dijkstra algorithm, we get the optimal route for emergency personnel.
units.reusable_pattern: According to [source], we get [output]. According to [method], we get [output]. Through [model], we found [output]. Based on [method], we get [output].
reusable_elements: occurrences: section 1.3.
stable function: preview every deliverable as a we-get sentence.
pattern: according to / through / based on, each ending in we get.
boundary: four outputs, no more; each must exist later.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add a fifth we-get for work the paper does not do.

units.function: promise that every simplifying assumption comes with a reason

original_instantiations: The simplifications below are there to shrink the problem, and every one of them carries its own reason.
What follows is a short list of simplifications, each paired with the reason it was allowed.

units.source_excerpt: We make the following basic assumptions in order to simplify the problem. Each of our assumptions is justified.
units.reusable_pattern: We make the following basic assumptions in order to simplify the problem. Each of our assumptions is justified.
information_order: promise of a reason per item
reusable_elements: occurrences: section 2.1, opening.
stable function: frame a bullet list of assumptions as reasoned, not arbitrary.
pattern: in order to simplify / each is justified.
boundary: the promise binds; an assumption with no reason breaks it.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim the assumptions are justified when the bullets give no reason.

units.function: credit a published method, then say the paper improves it and uses the improved form

original_instantiations: We cite and reference the search method of a paper on crowded evacuation and improve it, and use the improved version to pick the best escape route.
We take a published search method for dense crowds, change it, and run the changed version to choose the route out.

units.source_excerpt: We cite and reference the ant colony optimization algorithm of "Mathematical model of emergency evacuation in densely populated areas and its optimal solution" [5] and improve it, and use the improved ant colony optimization algorithm to select the optimal escape route.
units.reusable_pattern: We cite and reference [the method] of [the source] and improve it, and use the improved [method] to [the task].
reusable_elements: occurrences: section 3.2, opening.
stable function: locate the novelty as a modification, not a new method.
pattern: cite and reference / and improve it / and use.
boundary: the improvement must be visible in the next equation.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call a threshold tweak a new algorithm family.

units.function: restate the textbook principle, then show why it fails for people and forces a change

original_instantiations: The idea is that the shorter route draws more of the marker, so more and more agents pile onto it. But for people leaving a building this will happen: they reach a passage, see it full, and pick a quieter one to avoid a crush. So the method needs a change.
Shorter routes collect more of the signal and attract more agents. For a crowd that is the wrong outcome, because a full passage is exactly what people step away from. So we change the rule.

units.source_excerpt: The principle of traditional ant colony optimization algorithm is that the ants with shorter routes release more pheromone. Eventually, ants will focus on the best route under positive feedback. But for the evacuation of people, this situation will happen: when people reach one end of the channel and find that there are many people in the channel, people may choose another channel with fewer people. As a result, we need to improve the ant colony optimization algorithm.
units.reusable_pattern: The principle is that [the textbook behavior]. But for [our case], this situation will happen: [the failure]. As a result, we need to improve [the method].
reusable_elements: occurrences: section 3.2.1, closing paragraph.
stable function: motivate a modification by a concrete crowd behavior.
pattern: the principle is that / but for / this situation will happen / as a result.
boundary: the doubled sentence in the source is a slip; the move is the but-clause.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim the textbook method is wrong outside this setting.

units.function: define a threshold by what each side of it means in words

original_instantiations: When the marker level is below the cutoff, the passage holds few people and perhaps is not the best way out. When it is above the cutoff, the passage is the one more likely to jam.
Below the cutoff the passage is quiet, and may not be the route we want. Above it, the passage is where a jam is likely.

units.source_excerpt: When the pheromone concentration is lower than the threshold, it means that the number of people in the channel is small. Perhaps this route is not the optimal escape route; when the pheromone concentration is higher than the threshold, it means that the channel is more likely to occur congestion and blocking.
units.reusable_pattern: When [the signal] is lower than the threshold, it means [reading A]; when it is higher, it means [reading B].
reusable_elements: occurrences: section 3.2.2, first paragraph.
stable function: give a cutoff two plain-language meanings before the formula.
pattern: when lower than / it means / when higher than / it means.
boundary: both readings must match the formula that follows.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the cutoff without stating which side does what.

units.function: derive the clearance time as the longest last-person time, then define the shortest as its minimum

original_instantiations: We work out that the time to clear everyone is the time the last person gets out. The floor farthest from the doors must hold the stair that takes longest. So the clearance time is that longest last-person time, and the shortest clearance is the minimum of those longest times.
Clearing the building takes as long as the last person needs. Some stair will be the slowest. The clearance is that slowest time, and the best clearance is the smallest such slowest time.

units.source_excerpt: We figure out that the time required to evacuate all the visitors is the time when last visitor escapes. Moreover, the farthest floor is the 2nd floor. As a result, there must be a stairway that allows visitors from this stairway to evacuate for the longest time. The shortest evacuation time is the minimum of the longest time.
units.reusable_pattern: We figure out that [the total] is [the last unit]. As a result, there must be [one element] that takes the longest. The shortest [total] is the minimum of the longest.
information_order: the total as a last-unit time
reusable_elements: occurrences: section 3.3, opening.
stable function: justify a min-max objective in speech before the formula.
pattern: we figure out that / as a result, there must be / the minimum of the longest.
boundary: the min and the max must both be visible in the equation.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not apply min-of-max where the paper uses a plain sum.

units.function: assert that a capacity cap holds regardless of the crowd outside it

original_instantiations: No matter how crowded it is outside the stair, the number who pass through at once is just the width of the stair, so the queue can be treated as that many people abreast.
However full the landing gets, only as many as the stair can hold go through at one time, so the line reduces to that width.

units.source_excerpt: No matter how crowded outside the stairway, when passing through the stairway, the number of people passing through the stairway is just nf, so the human chain can be equivalent to the nf personal chain.
units.reusable_pattern: No matter how [extreme the outside], when [passing the constraint], the number is just [the cap], so [the reduction].
reusable_elements: occurrences: section 3.3, before equation (4).
stable function: license replacing a crowd by a fixed-width chain.
pattern: no matter how / is just / so ... can be equivalent to.
boundary: the cap must be a physical width, not a guess.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not use this to ignore crowding everywhere; it only caps the stair.

units.function: warn that a jam is the likely case, then narrate the two flows that cause it

original_instantiations: The following situation is easy to occur: people from the upper floor have already reached the stair, and the people on the lower floor have not yet left it, and finally a jam forms.
This case comes up readily. The floor above arrives at the stair while the floor below is still on it, and the stair blocks.

units.source_excerpt: The following situation is easy to occur: visitors on the 2nd floor have reached the 1st floor stairs, and visitors on the 1st floor have not escaped from this stairway, and finally blockage will occur.
units.reusable_pattern: The following situation is easy to occur: [flow A] has reached [the point], and [flow B] has not left it, and finally [the failure].
reusable_elements: occurrences: section 3.3, the blockage bullets.
stable function: motivate a congestion term with a two-flow story.
pattern: is easy to occur / and finally.
boundary: the story must match the sign of the delay term.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not treat every shared stair as blocked; the paper gives a condition.

units.function: break a tie between two flows by declaring a priority rule

original_instantiations: We assume that when this happens there is a priority, that is, the upper floor lets the lower floor go first.
When the two flows meet we give the lower floor the right of way.

units.source_excerpt: We assume that when the above situation occurs, there is a priority, that is, the higher floor allows the lower floor visitors to go first.
units.reusable_pattern: We assume that when [the conflict] occurs, there is a priority, that is, [who yields to whom].
reusable_elements: occurrences: section 3.3, before equation (7).
stable function: turn an ambiguous merge into a directed rule.
pattern: there is a priority, that is.
boundary: say which side waits; a priority with no direction is empty.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present the priority as observed behavior; it is assumed.

units.function: collapse two flows into one by an equivalence so the model stays small

original_instantiations: We look at the route and find the stair from the ground floor up is not the same stair the top floor uses. Therefore, people going from the ground floor up can be treated as equivalent to people coming down from the top.
The two stairs are different, so the ground-floor flow can stand in for a second top-floor flow and the model keeps two levels.

units.source_excerpt: We observe the escape route, and find that the stairs from the 0th floor to the 1st floor is different from the stairs from the 2nd floor to the 1st floor. Therefore, visitors escape from 0F to 1F can be equivalent to visitors escape from the 2nd floor to the 1st floor.
units.reusable_pattern: We observe [the layout], and find that [A] is different from [B]. Therefore, [flow A] can be equivalent to [flow B].
reusable_elements: occurrences: section 3.3, the three-floor reduction.
stable function: shrink the number of cases by a stated equivalence.
pattern: we observe and find / therefore ... can be equivalent to.
boundary: the equivalence needs the difference it rests on.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not merge flows that share a stair; the move depends on them not sharing one.

units.function: fold several exits into one because their channels match in length

original_instantiations: Two of the doors share one passage, and the third needs a stair of the same length. As a result, the three doors can be treated as one new door, and the number through it is the sum of the three.
The doors are the same length of travel apart, so we replace them by a single door whose width is their widths added.

units.source_excerpt: The entrance to the pyramid requires a stairway on the 2nd basement, which is the same length as the other two exit channels. As a result, three exits can be equivalent to a new exit. The number n' of people passing through the new exit is the sum of the three exits.
units.reusable_pattern: As a result, [several exits] can be equivalent to a new exit. The number passing through the new exit is the sum of [them].
reusable_elements: occurrences: section 3.3, the five-floor case.
stable function: collapse identical-length exits before computing time.
pattern: as a result ... can be equivalent to a new exit.
boundary: only merge exits whose travel length really matches.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not merge exits of different lengths.

units.function: compare the computed time with a stated maximum, then conclude the model works

original_instantiations: The best clearance differs by emergency, but the maximum cannot pass 15 minutes. The time the method gives is realistic and short. Therefore, the model works well.
Anything over 15 minutes is too long. Our number is under that and short, so we say the model works.

units.source_excerpt: According to the information, the best evacuation time for different emergencies is different, but the maximum can not exceed 15 minutes. The shortest evacuation time obtained by the algorithm is realistic and short. Therefore, our model works well.
units.reusable_pattern: The maximum can not exceed [the benchmark]. The [result] obtained by the algorithm is realistic and short. Therefore, our model works well.
reusable_elements: occurrences: section 3.3, closing.
stable function: close a computation against an external time limit.
pattern: can not exceed / realistic and short / therefore works well.
boundary: name the benchmark; realistic alone is not a test.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not treat under-15-minutes as validation for every building.

units.function: reject one option because it adds danger, then name the best way

original_instantiations: Shutting a main door so that only the responders use it would slow everyone else and add risk. Better: give the responders a side door and leave the main doors to the crowd.
Reserving a main door for the incoming team alone costs too much time. Hand them a spare door instead.

units.source_excerpt: If seal off the original exit and only allow the emergency personnel to enter, it will greatly increase the evacuation time and cause danger. The best way is to open one of other exits for emergency personnel, and visitors still evacuate from the four main entrances.
units.reusable_pattern: If [the tempting option], it will greatly increase [the cost] and cause danger. The best way is to [the alternative].
reusable_elements: occurrences: section 3.4, opening.
stable function: choose between two uses of a door by naming the danger.
pattern: it will greatly increase / the best way is.
boundary: the danger must be stated, not implied.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call an option best without saying what it beats.

units.function: recast the building as a graph whose edges change with time

original_instantiations: We think of the building as a graph whose passages change over time, and we think of the response team as a node whose position moves with time.
The building becomes a graph with edges that appear and vanish, and the responders are a node that travels on it.

units.source_excerpt: We think of the Louvre as a topology G(N, R(t)) changing over time where N is the node set, R(t) is the route set that changes over time. At the same time, we think of the emergency personnel as a node whose position move with time.
units.reusable_pattern: We think of [the place] as [a structure] changing over time. At the same time, we think of [the agent] as a node whose position moves with time.
reusable_elements: occurrences: section 3.4.
stable function: introduce a dynamic graph in speech.
pattern: we think of X as / at the same time, we think of Y as.
boundary: say what changes with time; a static graph does not earn this.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not use this phrasing for a graph that never changes.

units.function: hand the procedure to a flow chart instead of narrating every step

original_instantiations: We use the improved shortest-path method to find the best route for the response team. The specific process is as follows.
The improved path method gives the responders their route. The steps are in the chart.

units.source_excerpt: We use the improved Dijkstra's Algorithm to calculate the optimal route for emergency personnel to the emergency area. The specific process is as follows.
units.reusable_pattern: We use [the method] to calculate [the output]. The specific process is as follows.
reusable_elements: occurrences: section 3.4, before Figure 5.
stable function: delegate a procedure to a flow chart.
pattern: the specific process is as follows.
boundary: a figure must actually follow.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not point to a process that is never shown.

units.function: feed two values into the model and report that both give the same route

original_instantiations: Both arrival times go into the model and come back out as one and the same route.
Feeding the two later arrival times through the model changes nothing about which route wins.

units.source_excerpt: We set T as 180 and 150, and bring them into our model. The shortest route we get is the same and showed in the following figure.
units.reusable_pattern: We set [the input] as [values], and bring them into our model. The [output] we get is the same.
reusable_elements: occurrences: section 3.4, the worked example.
stable function: show a result is stable across two inputs.
pattern: we set / bring them into our model / the route we get is the same.
boundary: sameness is the claim; show the figure.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim stability beyond the values tested.

units.function: close a case comparison by picking the threshold the cases imply

original_instantiations: From the calculations, we choose the cutoff value of 141.
The cases point to one cutoff, and we set it at 141.

units.source_excerpt: According to the calculations, we choose the value of threshold T = 141.
units.reusable_pattern: According to the calculations, we choose the value of [the threshold].
reusable_elements: occurrences: section 3.4, closing line.
stable function: end a comparison with one selected number.
pattern: according to the calculations, we choose.
boundary: the number must sit between the cases just computed.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present the cutoff as fitted; it is read off four cases.

units.function: rank one action above the instinctive one for a group in a crisis

original_instantiations: Group or lone visitor, the priority is to leave immediately and split up, rather than delay until everyone has regrouped.
Staying together until the party is complete wastes the best window. Scatter and move.

units.source_excerpt: Whether it is a group or an individual to visit, when an emergency occurs, the most important thing to do is to quickly escape breaking up the whole into parts instead waiting for the group to gather and then evacuate which may miss the best escape time.
units.reusable_pattern: Whether [case A] or [case B], when [the event] occurs, the most important thing to do is to [the action] instead of [the instinct].
reusable_elements: occurrences: section 3.5.1, tourist groups.
stable function: override a natural behavior with a ranked instruction.
pattern: the most important thing to do is / instead of.
boundary: name the behavior being replaced.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not rank actions the model never represents.

units.function: translate a real-world factor into the one term of the model it changes

original_instantiations: Many languages often leave some visitors unable to follow the broadcast. In our model, it means the time to reach the stair grows.
When people cannot follow the announcement, the model shows it as a longer walk to the stair.

units.source_excerpt: The languages diversity often leads some visitors to fail to understand the instructions of emergency broadcasters and evacuation personnel. In our model, it means that the time to reach the stairway increases.
units.reusable_pattern: [The real factor] often leads to [the effect]. In our model, it means that [one term] increases.
information_order: the model term it maps to
reusable_elements: occurrences: section 3.5.1, languages.
stable function: connect a soft factor to a single equation term.
pattern: in our model, it means that.
boundary: map to one term; do not spread the factor across the model.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim the factor was measured; here it is only mapped.

units.function: justify a set of measures by the origin of most of the visitors

original_instantiations: Considering that most visitors come from a few language regions, we set the following measures.
Most visitors share a handful of languages, so the measures below follow from that.

units.source_excerpt: Considering that most tourists are from European and American countries, we have established the following measures.
units.reusable_pattern: Considering that [the majority fact], we have established the following measures.
reusable_elements: occurrences: section 3.5.1, before the language bullets.
stable function: ground a policy list in one observed majority.
pattern: considering that / we have established the following.
boundary: the measures must serve the majority named.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not let the majority erase the visitors it leaves out.

units.function: keep the same method for a special population and say exactly which set changes

original_instantiations: For visitors who cannot use stairs, we still use the same search and change the graph, swapping the stairs in the route set for the accessible ones and the ordinary stair nodes for accessible ones.
The same search runs for people who need step-free routes; only the nodes and edges change, from ordinary stairs to accessible ones.

units.source_excerpt: We still use the ant colony optimization algorithm and modify the topology where N is the node set and R is route set. We changed the stairs in the path set R to the disabled stairs, and changed the ordinary stairway in the node set N to the disabled stairway.
units.reusable_pattern: We still use [the method] and modify [the structure]. We changed [element A] to [variant A] and [element B] to [variant B].
reusable_elements: occurrences: section 3.5.1, disabled visitors.
stable function: extend a model to a subgroup by editing its graph, not its equations.
pattern: we still use / we changed X to Y.
boundary: state both the speed and the capacity that change with the graph.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim the subgroup was simulated if only the graph was edited.

units.function: read a chart threshold and turn it into a necessity claim

original_instantiations: The time limit of 15 minutes is reached when the crowd hits 28000. Therefore, other doors have to be considered once the crowd reaches 28000.
At 28000 people the clearance hits the 15-minute line, so beyond that the extra doors are no longer optional.

units.source_excerpt: The prime time for emergency evacuation is 15 minutes when the number of visitors is 28000. Therefore, it's necessary to consider other exit points when the number of visitors is 28000.
units.reusable_pattern: [The limit] is [the benchmark] when [the input] is [the value]. Therefore, it's necessary to [the action] when [the input] is [the value].
reusable_elements: occurrences: section 3.5.2, after Figure 11.
stable function: convert a chart crossing into an operational trigger.
pattern: therefore it's necessary to consider.
boundary: the trigger value must be read from the figure, not chosen.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not move the trigger to a round number the figure does not show.

units.function: dismiss a standing objection by pointing at the extra security a surge brings

original_instantiations: Crowds jump on free days and special shows, and the venue already adds guards for exactly that. So the side doors are staffed, not exposed.
The busy days are planned days, with extra guards already rostered, which takes the sting out of opening a side door.

units.source_excerpt: The surge in visitors is usually due to some reasons such as free ticket opening, special exhibitions and so on. The Louvre will strengthen security forces to prevent a stampede. Therefore, there is no need to worry about the safety of other exit points.
units.reusable_pattern: [The event] is usually due to [known causes]. [The operator] will [the countermeasure]. Therefore, there is no need to worry about [the objection].
reusable_elements: occurrences: section 3.5.2.
stable function: remove a security objection before using the extra doors.
pattern: therefore, there is no need to worry about.
boundary: the dismissal rests on the countermeasure; without it the worry stands.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not dismiss a security concern without a stated countermeasure.

units.function: reduce a whole class of threats to one edit of the graph

original_instantiations: A threat either blocks a passage or blocks a stair. As a result, we only need to edit the node set and the route set, and the new map and its time follow.
Blocked passages and blocked stairs are the two consequences, so changing the nodes and the edges is enough to get the new plan.

units.source_excerpt: There are two consequences of potential threats: some channels cannot pass, some staircase is not accessible. As a result, we only need to modify the node set N and route set R, then we can get the new evacuation map.
units.reusable_pattern: There are [two] consequences of [the threat]. As a result, we only need to modify [the structure], then we can get [the new result].
reusable_elements: occurrences: section 3.5.3.
stable function: show a threat class is already covered by the existing model.
pattern: as a result, we only need to modify.
boundary: the edit must be one the model already supports.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim threats outside the two consequences are covered.

units.function: open a recommendation list by saying the policies correspond to the model

original_instantiations: We have developed corresponding policies for the venue.
The policies below correspond to what the model found.

units.source_excerpt: We have developed corresponding policies for the Louvre.
units.reusable_pattern: We have developed corresponding policies for [the client].
reusable_elements: occurrences: section 4, opening.
stable function: tie a recommendation list back to the model.
pattern: we have developed corresponding policies.
boundary: each bullet should trace to a result; drills and training do not.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call a policy corresponding when no result supports it.

units.function: carry the method to other buildings by listing the data they must supply first

original_instantiations: For other large, crowded buildings, we can still use the improved search to get the best route out. First it is necessary to compute the number, length and width of stairs, passages and areas on each floor.
The same improved search works for other crowded buildings, but first someone has to count the stairs, passages and areas, floor by floor.

units.source_excerpt: For other large, crowded structures, we still can use the improved ant colony optimization algorithm to get the optimal evacuation route. First, it is necessary to calculate basic data such as the number, length, and width of stairways, passages, and areas of each floor.
units.reusable_pattern: For other [structures], we still can use [the method]. First, it is necessary to [the data they must provide].
reusable_elements: occurrences: section 5, opening.
stable function: offer portability while naming its price.
pattern: we still can use / first, it is necessary.
boundary: list the data; do not claim the method transfers for free.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not say the model applies anywhere without the data list.

units.function: separate two reasons the responders differ from the crowd

original_instantiations: On the one hand, the response team is usually small, so their own crowding rarely matters. On the other hand, they usually climb while the crowd descends, so the two must not meet.
The responders are few, so they do not jam each other. They also move upward against a crowd moving down, which is the collision to avoid.

units.source_excerpt: On the one hand, the number of emergency personnel is usually not particularly large, and it is usually not necessary to consider whether or not they will be congested. On the other hand, emergency personnel usually need to reach the high floors from the lower floors, avoiding collisions and crowding with people evacuating from the high floors.
units.reusable_pattern: On the one hand, [reason one]. On the other hand, [reason two].
information_order: why their own congestion is minor
reusable_elements: occurrences: section 5, third paragraph.
stable function: justify a different algorithm for the incoming team.
pattern: on the one hand / on the other hand.
boundary: two reasons, each doing different work.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not use the pair for two reasons that say the same thing.

units.function: redefine scenario questions as swings in one parameter

original_instantiations: Plenty of what-if questions come up while running an evacuation plan. What-if questions show up as swings in an important parameter. So we take two of them and test both at once.
The what-ifs are really just two parameters moving, so we vary those two and read the effect.

units.source_excerpt: There must be a lot of "What if" scenarios happen when performing evacuation plans. "What if" scenarios can be reflected in the fluctuation of important parameter of our model. Therefore, we will list two important "What if" scenarios and do sensitive analysis at the same time.
units.reusable_pattern: "What if" scenarios can be reflected in the fluctuation of [a parameter]. Therefore, we will list [two] and do sensitivity analysis at the same time.
reusable_elements: occurrences: section 6, opening.
stable function: frame a sensitivity section as answering spoken questions.
pattern: what if / can be reflected in the fluctuation / at the same time.
boundary: each what-if must name its parameter.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call two one-at-a-time sweeps a full sensitivity study.

units.function: read a figure as a large effect, then give the operational consequence

original_instantiations: The curve is steep: walking pace dominates the clearance time. On the day, stewards should push the pace while still preventing a crush.
Clearance time swings hard with pace, so the practical advice is to keep people moving briskly and safely.

units.source_excerpt: It can be seen that the effect of speed on evacuation time is very large. Therefore, in the actual evacuation process, the staff should guide the tourists to run as fast as possible while paying attention to safety.
units.reusable_pattern: It can be seen that the effect of [the parameter] on [the output] is very large. Therefore, in the actual process, [the operator] should [the action].
reusable_elements: occurrences: section 6, after Figure 15.
stable function: turn a steep curve into an instruction.
pattern: it can be seen that / is very large / therefore ... should.
boundary: the magnitude is visual; do not quote a slope the figure lacks.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not attach a percentage to a figure that shows none.

units.function: claim adaptability by pointing at the range of threats the model can take

original_instantiations: Our model is an adaptive one, and can be set up to handle a wide set of considerations and many kinds of threat.
The model adapts: the same frame takes a broad set of constraints and several threat types.

units.source_excerpt: Our model is an adaptive model, that can be designed to address a broad set of considerations and various types of potential threats.

stable function: summarize flexibility as the first strength.
pattern: an adaptive model, that can be designed to address.
boundary: the breadth must match the cases actually run.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim adaptability beyond the edits the paper demonstrates.

units.function: admit a uniform assumption, then give the numbers that show it is rough

original_instantiations: To simplify the calculation, we simply assume one thickness, one width and one speed for every visitor. In fact, we found that about 10 percent are children and 13 percent are elderly, about a quarter together, and that number is still fairly large.
We gave every person the same size and the same speed to keep the arithmetic small. The data say roughly a quarter are children or elderly, which is too many to ignore.

units.source_excerpt: For our model, to simplify the calculation, we simply assume the thickness and width of each visitor and the running speed. In fact, we found through information that in 2018, about 10% of tourists are children, and 13% of tourists are elderly people, accounting for about a quarter of the total, and the number is still relatively large.
units.reusable_pattern: To simplify the calculation, we simply assume [the uniform values]. In fact, we found that [the split], and the number is still relatively large.
reusable_elements: occurrences: section 7.2, first bullet.
stable function: weaken one's own assumption with the data that contradict it.
pattern: to simplify / we simply assume / in fact, we found / still relatively large.
boundary: give the numbers; a bare admission is weaker.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not soften the admission; the paper calls the share relatively large.

units.function: concede missing data and name the result it could change

original_instantiations: Measurements for several staircases were simply not available, and the true clearance time could shift because of it.
A handful of stair dimensions are missing, which leaves the computed clearance open to error.

units.source_excerpt: For some stairs, we are unable to obtain the corresponding data. This may affect the actual evacuation time.
units.reusable_pattern: For some [elements], we are unable to obtain the corresponding data. This may affect [the result].
reusable_elements: occurrences: section 7.2, third bullet.
stable function: bound a result by the data that are missing.
pattern: we are unable to obtain / this may affect.
boundary: name which result moves; do not apologize in general.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not extend the gap to data the paper does have.

units.function: retell the whole paper as a sequence of verbs

original_instantiations: At first, we get the crowd at each hour from the queue times the app shows. Then, we use the improved search for the best route and a time model for the shortest clearance at the largest crowd. Meanwhile, the improved path method gets the response team to the area. Finally, we test the two parameters the result leans on.
First the hourly crowd, then the route and the clearance time, meanwhile the responders' route, and finally the two parameters tested.

units.source_excerpt: At first, we get different numbers of people at different times of the day according to the current queuing time displayed by the APP. Then, we use the improved ant colony optimization algorithm to get the optimal evacuation route, and establish the Time Model to get the shortest evacuation time. Meanwhile, we use the improved Dijkstra algorithm for emergency personnel. Finally, we performed sensitivity analysis on two important parameters.
units.reusable_pattern: At first, [step one]. Then, [step two]. Meanwhile, [step three]. Finally, [step four].
reusable_elements: occurrences: section 8.
stable function: close by replaying the work in verb order.
pattern: at first / then / meanwhile / finally.
boundary: every verb must match a section that exists.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add a step in the recap that the body never did.
